title: A recording with no words
note: A kept recording that came back with no words shows the app's own small note, "No words in this one. The recording is kept just as it is.", muted sans with a microphone: not in the letter's type and with no "From ..." signature under it. The recording may hold laughing or babble, so the note never says nobody spoke. It counts as a letter once kept.
text: Asha's book Read together This month 7 October 31 to November 29 Month 6 3 letters · From Mama September 30 to October 30 Thursday, October 29, 2026 No words in this one. The recording is kept just as it is. Private 0:18 Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Bath time. You splash with your whole body, both hands, both feet, and then you check that I saw. Thursday, October 8, 2026 You rolled over all by yourself, twice, and then looked at me like you had always known how. From Mama Private 0:42 Month 5 1 letter · From Mama August 31 to September 29 Monday, August 31, 2026 So it rained all morning so we sat by the window and you tried to catch the drops on the glass. You were so serious about it. From Mama 0:42 Month 3 1 letter · From Mama June 30 to July 30 Sunday, July 19, 2026 You smell like warm milk and the lavender soap Papa insists on. I could sit here all night. From Mama Month 2 1 letter · From Mama May 31 to June 29 Wednesday, June 3, 2026 You laughed today. A real one. It sounded like a little hiccup that surprised you as much as it surprised me. From Mama 0:42 The first weeks 1 letter · From Mama March 31 to April 29 Saturday, April 18, 2026 Asha, you are four days old and the whole house is quiet. Your Nani made dal and nobody ate it because we were all watching you sleep. From Mama 0:42 Tonight Book Family
lines: No words in this one. The recording is kept just as it is.
Bath time. You splash with your whole body, both hands, both feet, and then you check that I saw.
You rolled over all by yourself, twice, and then looked at me like you had always known how.
So it rained all morning so we sat by the window and you tried to catch the drops on the glass. You were so serious about it.
You smell like warm milk and the lavender soap Papa insists on. I could sit here all night.
You laughed today. A real one. It sounded like a little hiccup that surprised you as much as it surprised me.
Asha, you are four days old and the whole house is quiet. Your Nani made dal and nobody ate it because we were all watching you sleep.
